title: Amphibious Aircraft Ontology — design parameter
description: A design parameter: an engineering quantity with a canonical definition, a unit, a measurement convention, and links to the regulatory symbols it corresponds to. constraints/ encodes what the regulation requires; it does not say what the quantities in those formulas correspond to in a design tool. 14 CFR 25.527 uses beta; a parametric model has deadrise_fwd and deadrise_aft. This layer is the join. Normative and enforced by tools/validate.py; schema/README.md carries the rationale.

id.description: Stable slug, e.g. deadrise-at-keel. Unique across the WHOLE corpus, constraints included — a mapping cites both the same way.

kind.description: `note` marks an entry that is not a quantity a tool holds — a recorded consequence of modelling, kept next to the parameter it concerns. Notes are exempt from implementation-coverage checks, since there is nothing for a tool to declare.

aliases.description: Other names in use for the same quantity, so a tool author searching for their own spelling lands here.

quantity.description: Units are QUDT IRIs, not strings — RDF/OWL, so usable directly by a reasoner, and cross-referenced to UCUM, UNECE and IEC 61360. Units are NEVER encoded in parameter names.

symbol.description: CPACS-style bracket form — "deg", "m", "1". Checked against the unit's record in units/.

definition.description: What the quantity IS, independent of any tool.

measurement_convention.description: HOW the quantity is measured. Two tools can agree on a definition and still disagree on a value if they measure at different stations or from different datums.

bounds.description: Canonical validity bounds, as distinct from any one tool's search range. Requires bounds_basis, because a bound with no stated authority gets enforced as though it had one.

bounds_basis.description: regulatory — the rule states it. mathematical — outside this range a governing expression is singular or undefined. conceptual — a sanity range carrying no authority, to be reported and NOT enforced as a rejection. Rejecting a valid unusual design is the failure mode this corpus exists to avoid.

distinct_from.description: Parameter ids this one is routinely and wrongly conflated with. The reason the layer exists; checked to resolve, so a rename cannot silently drop the warning.

implementations.description: Where the quantity appears in a published source: a report, a standard, a dataset, or a tool anyone can read. Descriptive, not normative. Only public sources are recorded, since a claim about a private tool is one no reader can check.

constraint.description: Constraint id in constraints/. Checked to resolve.

symbol.description: The symbol as it appears in that constraint.

relationship.description: identical — same quantity, same convention. discretization — the tool samples a continuous regulatory quantity. subset — the tool value applies over part of the regulatory domain. derived — computed from, not equal to. selects — the value determines WHICH regulatory case applies.

caveats.description: REQUIRED by tools/validate.py when relationship is not `identical`. A mapping that is not identical claims the two differ; unexplained, it is worse than no mapping.

system.description: The public source, named so a reader can find it, e.g. "NACA ARR 4F15 (Davidson & Locke 1944)".

identifier.description: The name that system uses. null when the parameter is absent there.

unit.description: QUDT IRI as that system uses it.

bounds.description: The ranges that source declares, keyed by what KIND of range each one is. A search box and a validity limit are different claims, and comparing one against the other reports a conflict that is not there.

validity.description: The range the system declares admissible. Outside it a value is refused, or reported as invalid, unless `basis` marks that end `conceptual`, in which case it is reported and accepted.

search.description: An optimiser's or trade study's box. Deliberately narrower than validity; a design outside it is unusual, not invalid.

tested.description: The span a test programme or dataset actually covered. Says where evidence exists, not what is permitted.

status.description: exact — the identifier means this parameter and nothing else. collapsed — one identifier stands for two or more parameters. conflated — the identifier is used where a DIFFERENT parameter belongs. renamed — same meaning, different spelling. absent — the system does not carry it.

finding.description: What the divergence costs, where it costs anything.

range.description: A range as a source states it: either end may be open, and either end may be exclusive. The same shape serves the canonical bounds and every kind of tool range, so the two compare field by field.

basis.description: The authority for each end, where the source states one, in the vocabulary of bounds_basis. An end marked `conceptual` is reported by that tool, not refused. Left out when the source states no basis.
